subject: Data jurisdiction routing & DPA: operator/subprocessor mapping and timeline
messages:
From: Anna Schultz <anna.schultz@supplyhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@supplyhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA routing / transfer impact addendum

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement and legal have a couple of outstanding questions before we can sign the Order Form + DPA:

1) Role mapping: we currently classify SupplyHealth as a joint controller for the patient data schema. Redwood’s DPA marks you as processor. Can you confirm if you will accept a processor-only relationship for the features in the Order Form, or will you require controller-to-controller clauses for specific data types?

2) Subprocessors: we need the current subprocessor list and whether Redwood can commit to 30-days notice before onboarding any new EU subprocessor.

3) Cross-border routing: We operate in the EU and UK — we need clarity on whether requests originating in EU will be routed through EU-only capacity or could be routed to Redwood-hosted US capacity. If routing to non-EU will occur, we need an explicit transfer impact addendum and the SCCs version you rely on.

4) Key management: can you support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) for encryption-at-rest for EU tenants?

Can you loop in whoever handles the technical routing and the DPA redlines? We’d like a readout by Friday EOD 7/27 to keep the procurement window open.

Thanks,
Anna Schultz
Head of Privacy & Compliance
SupplyHealth

--
Attachment: SH-DPA-questions-070828.pdf (list of specific clause asks)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schultz <anna.schultz@supplyhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA routing / transfer impact addendum

Anna —

Appreciate the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Monica (privacy ops). High level responses inline below; we attached our redlined DPA and a short processing map for review.

- Role mapping: For the features in the order form we operate as a processor; where SupplyHealth triggers data enrichment that creates derived product metrics, we’re open to discussing limited joint-controller language for that specific flow, but need to scope it precisely.

- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor roster. We can commit to 30-days notice for new subprocessors for EU data, with the exception of transient CDN providers (we’ll flag those).

- Routing: We have an EU-region hosting option. Default hosted order will route to nearest capacity; for EU-only routing we can pin the tenant to EU Dedicated pool (requires a config flag on the order form and a small uplift). If that’s acceptable, I’ll note it in the Order Form redline.

- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated customers; for hosted standard we offer Redwood-managed KMS with optional envelope encryption. I’ve asked Monica to outline the technical tradeoffs.

Action items and timeline (proposal):
- Laura/legal to review redline and propose controller/processor language (deadline: Thu 7/26 noon).
- Monica to confirm KMS options and uplift for EU-pinned capacity (Thu 7/26 EOD).
- Ben to produce a short mutual action plan and updated Order Form showing EU pin (Fri 7/27).

Attaching: SupplyHealth_DPA_bencar_redline_v3.docx, OrderForm_AnnexA_processing-map.xlsx

Best,
Ben
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: SupplyHealth_DPA_bencar_redline_v3.docx
Attachment: OrderForm_AnnexA_processing-map.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on DPA routing / transfer impact addendum

Thanks Ben — read the redline. Quick summary of legal’s position and suggested language.

1) Controller/processor: Our default stance for the MSA + Order Form is processor for all standard model inference features. For any non-standard data enrichment we will accept narrow joint-controller carve-outs limited to specific data classes and purposes; I propose the following language to insert into the DPA: 

"Where Customer and Redwood jointly determine that a specific processing activity results in joint determination of purposes and means, the parties shall execute a written annex specifying the data classes, purposes, and duration solely for that activity."

2) SCCs & transfer basis: We will adopt the EU Commission 2021 SCCs v2. Parties must indicate whether processing will rely on SCCs + additional technical safeguards (e.g., EU-pinned keys). If SupplyHealth requires a Transfer Impact Addendum, we can provide a standard addendum describing the technical and legal mitigations for routing to non-EU capacity.

3) Subprocessor notice: Accept 30-day notice for EU subprocessors; propose an exception list (CDNs, ephemeral infra) and an obligation to notify within 72 hours for any security-impacting changes.

4) KMS: We will require customer-managed KMS for EU-pinned Dedicated customers. For hosted accounts we can offer envelope keys with export controls clarified in the Order Form. Karthik — please confirm whether EU-pinned Dedicated can enforce KMS tenancy separation at the infra layer or if we need a contractual guarantee only.

Please see my tracked-changes summary (attached). I recommend we push for EU-pinning on the Order Form and a single-sentence uplift for pricing to avoid procurement delay. Target internal signoff Thursday EOD so Ben can share a clean package on Friday.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Laura_summary_trackedchanges.docx
From: Tom Reed <tom.reed@supplyhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Anna Schultz <anna.schultz@supplyhealth.com>
Cc: MintLaw LLP <legal@mintlaw.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Jul 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA routing / transfer impact addendum

Ben/Anna —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. MintLaw reviewed Redwood’s redline and Laura’s summary. A couple of counterpoints from our side to keep the deal on track: 

• Role mapping: Our procurement team is comfortable with processor treatment for all inference calls, provided SupplyHealth keeps full control over data classification decisions. We don’t want open-ended joint-controller annexes. Can Redwood accept a one-paragraph limitation that any joint-controller carve-out requires a written request and explicit internal sign-off?

• KMS & EU pin: We prefer customer-managed keys even for hosted if possible. If Redwood cannot offer CMK for hosted, we’ll accept Dedicated with EU pin but need a clear uplift number. Can you confirm uplift percentage and lead time?

• Routing/transfer impact: the counter-redline attaches proposed wording that requires Redwood to provide a transfer-impact addendum when routing out of EU, and to state the SCCs version in the DPA. We included a suggested sentence for 30-day subprocessor notice and a narrow exception list.

We attached the counter-redline as a PDF. Procurement is pushing for final terms by 7/31 so we can complete fiscal quarter procurement. Would Redwood be willing to lock pricing for 12 months if we sign by 7/31?

Tom Reed
Dir. Procurement
SupplyHealth

--
Attachment: SupplyHealth_counter-DPA-redline.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schultz <anna.schultz@supplyhealth.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@supplyhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Questions on DPA routing / transfer impact addendum

Team — quick summary and proposed MAP so we can close: 

1) Commercial compromise: Redwood will offer EU-pinned Dedicated with customer-managed KMS as the standard privacy-preserving option. Pricing uplift: +12% on committed throughput tiers; lead time for provisioning: ~2 weeks after PO. (Laura to confirm final billing language with finance.)

2) DPA redline: Laura to accept SupplyHealth’s 30-day notice with the proposed exception list and to include the SCCs v2 reference and a short transfer-impact addendum template. Laura — please produce a clean DPA & one-page summary by Mon 7/30 COB.

3) Order Form: Ben to add an explicit checkbox for "EU-pinned Dedicated + CMK" in Annex A and include a pricing row. Monica please confirm technical feasibility and whether any SOC evidence changes are required. Target updated Order Form for review Mon 7/30.

4) Docs & signatures: Tom — once the clean DPA + Order Form are ready we can send DocuSign. Ben is willing to lock pricing for 12 months if sign by 7/31; confirm and we’ll reflect in the Order Form.

Next steps / owners:
- Laura: clean DPA + transfer-impact addendum template (due Mon 7/30 COB).
- Monica: CMK feasibility + SOC evidence list (due Mon 7/30 EOD).
- Ben: Order Form checkbox + pricing row + DocuSign prep (due Mon 7/30).

If that timeline works I’ll package and send Friday evening so legal has a clean doc to review over the weekend.

Thanks —
Ben
